overall: Chair Dirsa violated the Open Meeting Law by emailing a quorum about public business; the Committee violated it by failing to timely respond to a complaint; the unnoticed-meeting claim was untimely; nullification was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee deliberated outside a meeting when the Chair emailed a quorum about a petition for exclusion.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Chair's January 10, 2012 email constituted an individual violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee held an unnoticed, illegal meeting on the exclusion petition, referenced in February 2012 minutes as an unofficial January meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint was filed on June 16, 2012; 116 days after the alleged violation could have been reasonably discovered.

allegations.summary: The Committee did not respond to the Open Meeting Law complaint filed with it within 14 business days, and only responded months later.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Committee failed to respond to Attorney McKenna's Open Meeting Law complaint within 14 business-days.

remedy: Order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Order the Committee members now serving to attend an Open Meeting Law training, or view the online training video, and certify to the AG within 60 days.
remedy_passage: we order the Committee members now serving to attend a training on the Open Meeting Law
